solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Queen goes to outskirts of city — one in France

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of England and Scotland

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters of the word city are kept

explanation.surface: A monarch sets off for the suburbs of a city somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' keeps CY, the outer letters of 'city'. 'one in France' is the definition: a French city, like the one just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Annecy is a lakeside town in the Haute-Savoie, so it is one French city among many.

clue.text: Cor! Maria is off to old Brittany

indicators.note: something that is off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise as Maria departs for ancient Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' looks like a cry of surprise, but it is just letters. 'is off' says to rearrange CORMARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorica was the Roman-era name for the region of north-west Gaul that became Brittany.

clue.text: Cathedral's title includes radical books first

indicators.note: one word including others holds them inside it

parts.note: a title is a name

indicators.note: first says the books come before the radical in the inserted string

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the usual crossword books
a radical is a Red, a political leftist

explanation.surface: A cathedral's name apparently contains radical scripture placed up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' is a political Red here, not an adjective for the books; 'first' fixes the order of the two inserted pieces, and 'includes' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame de Paris is the city's famous Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: Waterbird on edge of the Camargue also turned up

indicators.note: the leading edge of the word Camargue is its opening letter
in a down answer, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: A bird of the wetlands has appeared at the margin of the Camargue too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge of' gives C from Camargue, and 'turned up' reverses TOO to OOT beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The coot is a black waterbird of lakes and marshes, common in the Camargue.

clue.text: A trolley porter brought round with various dishes in 11

indicators.note: something brought round another surrounds it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so ale
a trolley is a cart

explanation.surface: A railway porter wheels a trolley round, laden with assorted dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' is the dark beer, not a railway worker, and 'brought round' is the container signal. Other clues use '11' (Reims) to mean French.
explanation.definitionFit: A la carte is French for ordering separately priced items from a full menu of dishes.

clue.text: Badly demoralised — no more little boys

indicators.note: badly means the letters of demoralised are put in poor order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: these letters are taken away, as no says

explanation.surface: Feeling terribly low and no longer able to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: 'no more' removes M, O, R, E from DEMORALISED, and 'Badly' rearranges the remaining DALISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddies is a Scots diminutive for young lads, hence little boys.

clue.text: Chef's unusual blunder — cook finally ousted

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of the word cook is thrown out

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A chef makes an odd mistake, and the cook is finally sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally ousted' drops K from COOK to leave COO; 'unusual' shuffles COO with BLUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon bleu is a cook of the highest class, so a top chef.

clue.text: Bears losing capital? Remains to be seen at Pont du Gard

definitions.text: Remains to be seen at Pont du Gard

indicators.note: losing its capital means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: bruins is an old word for bears

explanation.surface: Bears losing a city? Then a Roman monument in southern France turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing capital' drops the B of BRUINS. 'capital' tempts as a city; here it is the head letter. The Pont du Gard is a Roman aqueduct in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruins are the remains of old buildings, such as the Roman aqueduct at Pont du Gard.

clue.text: Tries art in 11 and declares

parts.note: art is the old second-person form of are; in French (11, Reims) tu es is thou art
to declare is to say

explanation.surface: Attempts at painting in Reims, and some announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is REIMS, so 'in 11' means in French: 'art' as in 'thou art' is French ES.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, so essays are tries.

clue.text: WW2 resistance forces run away from noble

indicators.note: the run is taken away from the nobleman's title

parts.note: a marquis is a nobleman
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Wartime resistance fighters flee from a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes R from MARQUIS. 'run away' reads as fleeing, but 'run' is the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maquis were rural guerrilla bands of the French Resistance in the Second World War.

clue.text: Urban area with underground lake, as well

parts.note: the Metro is an underground railway
L is a map abbreviation for lake
as well means and, in addition

explanation.surface: A city district boasting an underground railway and a lake too.
explanation.walkthrough: Metroland is the suburbs north-west of London that grew along the Metropolitan underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: Metroland names a suburban stretch built up around a railway line, a kind of urban area.

clue.text: Poor miser in French city

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A penniless skinflint living in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like it describes the miser but signals the rearrangement. Other clues use '11' to mean French.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is a cathedral city in Champagne, in north-east France.

clue.text: Regrets ways in 11

definitions.meaning: to regret something is to rue it
in French (11, Reims), rue means street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about the routes taken in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: The English verb means regrets; the French noun rue means street, and rues are ways.

clue.text: Queen's radio broadcast, for example, not far from 2

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of radio are spread about

parts.note: for example means say

explanation.surface: The monarch's radio address is given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges RADIO into AIDOR. The definition is cryptic: a Paris embankment a short walk along the Seine from Notre-Dame (2).
explanation.definitionFit: The Quai d'Orsay is a Paris riverside quay close to the Ile de la Cite and its cathedral.

clue.text: Frenchman not upset about going round market in part of Paris …

indicators.note: the letters built so far go round, enclosing, the next piece

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of not are rearranged

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A calm Frenchman strolls round a market in a Paris district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the word not, rather than reversing it; 'going round' is the container signal for the Frenchman, the shuffle and 'about' around the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Montmartre is the hilltop district of Paris famous for Sacre-Coeur and its artists.

clue.text: Mountain animal taking tea for a month in 11

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
in French (11, Reims) mois means month

explanation.surface: A mountain creature that has taken a month's supply of tea to Reims.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is REIMS, so 'in 11' means in French. CHA (char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a goat-antelope of the Alps and Pyrenees, a mountain animal.

clue.text: Footwear of French peasants, small monks but no bishop

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small

indicators.note: no bishop means the letter for bishop is left out

parts.note: abbots are senior monks
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Peasant shoes worn by little monks, though not by any bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops just one of the two Bs the monks' word holds; the other stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabots are the wooden clogs traditionally worn by French peasants.

clue.text: … decorator working in another part

indicators.note: working means the letters of decorator are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A decorator busy on a job in a different district of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue, so 'another part' means another part of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trocadero is a Paris district facing the Eiffel Tower across the Seine.

clue.text: Exams even grasped by fool

indicators.note: something grasped by another is held inside it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
even means level, flat

explanation.surface: Tests that even an idiot could get hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: AS levels are British school exams taken around age 17.
explanation.definitionFit: AS levels are British advanced subsidiary examinations, a set of exams.

clue.text: Like 21 across, Scottish football champions 2016-17

definitions.meaning: the Bretons are a ... people, so this means of that people
the Glasgow club that won the Scottish Premiership that season

explanation.surface: Like the people of Brittany, and a winning football team from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bretons speak a Celtic language; and Glasgow's Celtic won the Scottish title unbeaten in 2016-17.

clue.text: US city, fashionable in 11, in the past

parts.note: chic is French (11, Reims) for stylish, fashionable
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An American city that was once stylish in Reims.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is REIMS, so 'in 11' means in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major city in Illinois, in the United States.

clue.text: No. 27 confused 27's residents

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number, read here as the letters N and O
27 refers to the French port, the answer to 27 across

explanation.surface: A cross-reference muddle about the residents of a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 27' looks like a reference number, but NO is letters; 'confused' mixes them with BREST.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Brittany, where Brest lies, are Bretons.

clue.text: Swimmer turns blue, then turns silver

indicators.note: the first turns means the letters of blue are turned into a new order
the second turns means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A swimmer goes blue with cold and then pale silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'turns' rearranges BLUE to BELU; the second reverses AG to GA.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a white Arctic whale, and also a large sturgeon: either swims.

clue.text: Little Edith cut French corn that's fit to eat

indicators.note: cut means the end of the word is cut off

parts.note: Edie is a pet form of Edith
ble is French for wheat, corn

explanation.surface: Young Edith harvested some French corn that is good to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of EDIE, leaving EDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is safe and fit to be eaten.

clue.text: Drunk beside hall, looking unkempt

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy figure next to the hallway, looking dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges BESIDEHALL. 'beside' looks like a link word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Deshabille describes being carelessly or partly dressed, which looks untidy.

clue.text: Fragrance of early stocks — one hundred in 11

indicators.note: the early part of the word stocks is its opening letter

parts.note: cent is French (11, Reims) for a hundred

explanation.surface: The perfume of early-flowering stocks, a hundred of them in Reims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' takes S from 'stocks'. Stocks here look like the garden flower, a fitting decoy for a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a pleasant smell, a fragrance.

clue.text: Bargain time that's dirty in 11

definitions.meaning: a period when goods are sold cheaply

explanation.surface: A grubby clearance event held in Reims.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's sale is a time of bargains; the French adjective sale means dirty.

clue.text: Island mountain range

definitions.meaning: an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
the range along the French-Swiss border that names the Jurassic period

explanation.definitionFit: Jura is a Scottish Hebridean isle, and also the mountains straddling France and Switzerland.

clue.text: Leading battleships remain at French port

indicators.note: the leading letter of battleships is the one at its front

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Front-line warships stay at a French harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' takes B from 'battleships'. Brest is a major French naval base, so the warships fit the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a port and naval base at the western tip of Brittany.

clue.text: Capital of Charente, one right away from minor league revision

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A lower division is reorganised, with one right removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' takes I (one) and R (right) out of MINOR LEAGUE; 'revision' rearranges what is left, MNOLEAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Angouleme is the prefecture, the administrative capital, of the Charente department.

clue.text: Warehouse Parisian's in, little one containing cloth

parts.note: a Parisian says en for the English word in

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
rep is a ribbed fabric

explanation.surface: A storehouse where a Parisian lives, with a child holding fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian's in' asks for the French word for in; 'containing' is the container signal for the child and the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a port or depot where goods are stored for re-export, a warehouse.

clue.text: Lass troubled working at spa centres or lounges in 11

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A worried girl employed at health spas or in sitting rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' is the anagram signal. 'spa centres' looks like a containment hint but belongs to the definition: beauty salons, or French drawing rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Salons are beauty parlours like spa centres, and in French a salon is a lounge.
